title: Alien Nine
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a future where alien invasions are routine, Elementary School #9 makes three sixth-graders, timid Yuri, dutiful Kumi and enthusiastic Kasumi, its Alien Party, armed with symbiotic alien 'Borgs' worn on their heads. Cute art gives way to violent, unsettling body horror as the girls are changed by the aliens they fight. A 3-volume seinen manga by Hitoshi Tomizawa; first published in English by CPM, with a new edition announced by Peow2.
life_message: Growing up means being pushed into frightening change by adults, and keeping one's self through it.

content.note: Heavy violence despite child leads (Wikipedia); manga more graphic than the OVA (ANN); AniList Gore, MU Blood and Gore.
Body horror, cosmic horror and pervasive unease (AniList, MU, Wikipedia); a girl is absorbed by an alien.
Critics read rape and incest metaphors in the anime (Wikipedia, citing SFE); ANN says no lolicon pandering in the manga.
Kumi's depression (ANN); constant fear and crying (Wikipedia, MU Crybaby Protagonist, Mind Break).
Children ordered into combat; unlikely to imitate.

dominant: Fear of growing up; adult institutions using children; bodily change

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Girls endure assigned duty; no honor code or revenge.

Order vs freedom.evidence: School appoints the children and adults enforce duty (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Duty is to school and community; Kumi helps her widowed mother.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Teachers and the principal command children who must comply.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Security against aliens outweighs the girls' wishes.

folkways.japan: Class representatives chosen by vote and school duty imposed on children reflect Japanese school roles, described as context.

delivery.evidence: Critics call it an allegory for puberty under cute art (Wikipedia); ANN praises subtle dialogue.
delivery.note: Meaning is carried by metaphor and mood rather than stated.

winners_losers: The girls survive changed; Yuri alone stays fully human by refusing to merge with her Borg; sympathy rests with the children against the adults who use them.
to_verify: ANN review calls the girls junior high students; Wikipedia says sixth grade.
